title: 1951 AHSME Problem 33
statement: The roots of the equation \(x^2-2x=0\) can be obtained graphically by finding the abscissas of the points of intersection of each of the following pairs of equations except the pair:

solutions.text:
Choices A, B, D, and E all reduce their intersection condition to \(x^2-2x=0.\) Choice C instead requires \[ x=x-2, \] which has no solution and therefore cannot produce the desired roots.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Set the two right-hand sides in each pair equal
Four pairs reduce to \(x^2-2x=0\); one pair reduces to an impossible constant equation
